extracted.intended_audience: general public (employers, draft-eligible men, and policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: News report describing Selective Service instructions and priorities for employer-prepared replacement schedules, deferment review procedures, and related V-mail/photo rules affecting fathers and draft-eligible workers during wartime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release timing for deferred childless men
rubrics_metrics.description: The new instructions require that schedules filed after July 1 must provide for release of occupationally deferred childless men between 18 and 25 years old within six months unless their jobs are exceptionally important to the war effort and extremely difficult to fill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions allowed where jobs are exceptionally important to the war effort and extremely difficult to fill; applies to schedules filed after July 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement priority by training/replacement time
rubrics_metrics.description: “Generally speaking, those who will be replaced first will be chosen in occupations having the shortest training and replacement time.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers should list for replacement workers in occupations that can be most quickly retrained/replaced to minimize production disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of previous and existing deferments
rubrics_metrics.description: “Due consideration should be given to previous and existing periods of deferment.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing schedules, factor in men’s prior or current deferment lengths when deciding replacement order or renewed deferments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement priority by marital/parental status
rubrics_metrics.description: “Where men are equally replaceable, single men should be listed for release before childless married men, and the latter should be listed for release before fathers.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit tie-breaking priority: single → childless married → fathers when replaceability is equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiebreaker: draft-call number order
rubrics_metrics.description: “Where men of the same family status are equally replaceable, they should be listed for replacement in order (draft-call) number with lowest order number first.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If family status is the same and replaceability equal, use draft-call (order) numbers ascending as the tiebreaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing fathers on replacement schedules / deferment expiration cutoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Men in the class of fathers, hitherto omitted from replacement schedules because they were safeguarded by paternity deferment, are to be listed on schedules filed after July 1 unless the proposed deferment would expire 'before October'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes that drafting of fathers is inevitable; include fathers on schedules filed after July 1 unless their deferment ends prior to the stated cutoff (October).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and approval process for replacement schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers may file replacement schedules which, when approved by state Selective Service directors, set up timetables for replacement of draft-eligible workers in key posts so their induction will not hamper production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers file schedules; state directors approve and stamp forms to be sent to local draft boards requesting deferments in accordance with the schedule. Aim is to coordinate inductions with minimal production disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer ability to request occupational deferment
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement schedules may request occupational deferment (or renewals) for workers whose positions are considered essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedules can ask for occupational deferments and renewals; state directors review and approve schedules and local boards receive requests for individual deferments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local board authority and deferment review schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Local boards have authority to refuse deferment for any man, though in practice they seldom do. The boards must review within six months each deferment approved under replacement schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even after state approval, local boards can deny deferments; approved deferments require a review at least every six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: V-mail photo transmission rules for fathers overseas
rubrics_metrics.description: Fathers in the armed forces serving overseas may get, via V-mail, photographs of their offspring under 1 year old or born since dad left for overseas. The regulation V-mail form cannot be altered, and the photograph is limited in size (not more than [size cutoff in article]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photos must be transmitted on the official V-mail form without alteration and must meet size limits; intended to allow servicemen to receive photos of very young children or infants born after departure.
